articles.title: That Morning Soda Might Be Messing With Your Brain More Than You Think
articles.summary: A 16-year-old scientist found that caffeine can turn down important brain genes in young animals. Her experiments with fish and rat cells showed fewer brain connections and more anxious behavior. This could mean caffeine affects kids differently than adults.

articles.title: This New Solar Machine Makes Fuel From Thin Air—No Batteries Needed!
articles.summary: Scientists in Japan built a device that turns sunlight, water, and CO2 into fuel without any batteries. It uses a special self-adjusting part that gets more efficient as it heats up. The system worked outdoors and even powered a tiny model at a world expo.

articles.title: Polly Really Wants a Cracker—and She Might Know Your Name!
articles.summary: A big study of over 880 pet parrots found that many use names in ways that seem like how people do. Some birds even say their own name to get attention. Scientists think parrots might be smarter at social talk than we knew.
